item.title: Top Hong Kong gov’t adviser calls for end to civil servants’ pay freeze
item.description: Top adviser Jeffrey Lam has called on the Hong Kong government to end a pay freeze for civil servants imposed last year, citing an improved economic outlook. item.title: ‘Not about condoms’: Chinese shrug off new contraceptive tax
item.description: By Isabel Kua China has made condoms and other contraceptives more expensive as it tries to boost birth rates, but residents in Beijing and analysts say the measure will have little impact. Consumers must now pay a 13 percent value-added tax for contraception including condoms, after Beijing removed exemptions on the products from January 1. […]

item.title: Residents displaced by Tai Po fire must leave youth hostels by end of January
item.description: Residents displaced by the deadly Wang Fuk Court blaze have until the end of January to leave youth hostels designated for their temporary resettlement, authorities have confirmed. item.title: HKFP Lens: Hong Kong kicks off New Year with vibrant lion dances
item.description: More than 1,500 lion dance performers from across the globe gathered in Hong Kong last week for the 2026 Dragon and Lion Festival and the Eighth World Dragon and Lion Day. item.title: Ocean Park ride remains suspended 2 days after 15 trapped mid-air for 20 minutes
item.description: An Ocean Park ride has remained suspended – two days after a malfunction left people stranded mid-air for 20 minutes. item.title: Hong Kong prosecutors drop charges against surgeon with dementia in Botox death case
item.description: Hong Kong prosecutors have dropped 21 charges against a nonagenarian plastic surgeon after a court granted him an unconditional release for the unlawful killing of a patient due to his advanced dementia. item.title: Up to 11-hour waits at Hong Kong public hospitals at night despite fee hike
item.description: Accident and emergency (A&E) departments at Hong Kong public hospitals have seen long queues at night despite a fee increase taking effect last week, with non-urgent patients waiting up to 11 hours. item.description: Cold weather in Hong Kong will continue until Friday under the influence of the winter monsoon, according to the Observatory.
